overview: Medford Bites interviewed State Representative candidate Chris Oates, who discussed his background in political risk, his legislative priorities for housing and energy, and the need for more competition in the Massachusetts state house.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Background
items.summary: Chris Oates introduced his candidacy for the 34th Middlesex District and discussed his professional background in international relations, political risk analysis, and government transparency software.

items.title: Legislative Competitiveness in Massachusetts
items.summary: Oates critiqued the lack of contested races in the state legislature, arguing that uncontested elections lead to a culture of stagnation and lack of urgency on Beacon Hill.

items.title: Housing and Energy Priorities
items.summary: The candidate advocated for statewide zoning reform to lower housing costs and suggested incentivizing battery storage to improve the efficiency of solar energy.

items.title: School Enrollment and Long-term Planning
items.summary: Oates proposed that the legislature begin planning immediately for a projected 10 to 35 percent decline in student enrollment over the next 20 years to avoid future school budget crises.

items.title: Specific Legislative Proposals
items.summary: Proposed initiatives include implementing Alaska-style open primaries with ranked-choice voting, banning non-compete agreements, and re-legalizing happy hour.

items.title: Campaign Outreach and Candidate Distinction
items.summary: Oates announced a campaign kickoff on June 28 and argued that his policy experience distinguishes him from other candidates who have held local office.

subject: State Representative Candidate Chris Oates Interview
